page:
Introduction to core Zod workflow for new users. Covers schema definition, data parsing, error handling, and type inference. Curated one-time walk-through excluding edge cases and carve-outs. Entry point before comprehensive API documentation.
- Creating object schemas with z.object and primitive types
- Parsing data with .parse method returning deep clones
- Async parsing with .parseAsync for async refinements/transforms
- Error handling with try/catch and ZodError
- .safeParse for result object with discriminated union (success/error)
- .safeParseAsync for async error handling
- .validate for boolean validation without error building (up to 16x faster)
- .validateAsync for async schemas
- Type inference with z.infer<typeof schema>
- Input and output type distinction with z.input<> and z.output<>
- How do I define a basic Zod schema?
- How do I validate data against a schema?
- How do I handle validation errors?
- How do I extract TypeScript types from Zod schemas?

sections.manifest: Schema definition with z.object for object types. Basic example with string and number properties. Zod and Zod Mini imports. z.string, z.number primitive schemas. For complete API reference, see /api page.

Data parsing with .parse method validating input and returning strongly-typed deep clone. .parseAsync for async refinements/transforms. Note: async schemas require .parseAsync, synchronous .parse throws error.

Error handling for validation failures. .parse throws ZodError instance. ZodError.issues array with granular information: expected type, code (invalid_type), path, message. .safeParse returns discriminated union {success: false, error: ZodError} or {success: true, data: T}. .safeParseAsync for async error handling. .validate returns boolean (never builds error, up to 16x faster than .safeParse().success). .validateAsync for async schemas with validation.

Type inference extracting static types from schemas. z.infer<typeof schema> extracts output type. z.input<typeof schema> extracts input type. z.output<typeof schema> equivalent to z.infer. Used for divergent input/output types with transforms. Links to full schema API documentation.
